Mia (devex): heads-up: found a redaction gap in the Go sampleapp while onboarding a partner. debug logs print raw x-request-id when OTEL hooks are enabled even though REDACT_REQUEST_IDS=true
Sam L: ouch. which release of the sampleapp and SDK?
Mia (devex): sampleapp v0.9.2, using redwood/sdk-go v0.7.2. env printed at start: REDACT_REQUEST_IDS=true LOG_LEVEL=debug OTEL_ENABLED=1
Julian R: can you paste the exact log lines? quick guess: hook ordering or handler-level debug before middleware sanitizes header.
Mia (devex): excerpt below:
```
2026-03-21T09:12:10Z INFO  sampleapp v0.9.2 starting
ENV: REDACT_REQUEST_IDS=true LOG_LEVEL=debug OTEL_ENABLED=1
2026-03-21T09:12:11Z DEBUG http.server incoming request_id=8a7f2c33f4b9c2a3e8d9 path=/api/complete
2026-03-21T09:12:11Z DEBUG otel.span trace_id=aa11bb... request_id=8a7f2c33f4b9c2a3e8d9
```
Sam L: that matches the pattern. when log level is debug we have some extra instrumentation in the handler that logs headers directly.
Priya (eng-runtime): noted. in Python we fixed a similar problem by making the logging middleware wrap all handlers at the very outer layer (so it sanitizes early). maybe Go sampleapp registers logging too late.
Mia (devex): middleware order in sampleapp is: initOTel -> authMiddleware -> handlerWrapper (which sets up request context) -> handler. logging is implemented as a wrapper but only attached in the router after handlerWrapper. so handler debug logs can run before logging wrapper runs.
Julian R: two ways to fix: (A) move logging middleware to be the first wrapper so it runs on tcp accept, scrubs headers on r.Context(), and then passes on; or (B) add a small sanitization helper called at top of ServeHTTP that unconditionally redacts sensitive headers if REDACT_REQUEST_IDS is true.
Sam L: plan: short-term add sanitization in ServeHTTP + readme note. long-term change middleware ordering and add cross-language SDK contract tests.
Mia (devex): also raising an onboarding UX problem: the README for sampleapp doesn't mention the OTEL+REDACT interaction. new devs turning on debug will accidentally leak IDs into their local logs and might copy them into issues.
Priya (eng-runtime): I will open a runtime PR to reorder wrappers and add unit tests. also suggest adding a CI grep that fails the build if raw 32-char hex request IDs appear in logs when REDACT_REQUEST_IDS=true.
Julian R: add an SDK parity task for Go/Python/Node to ensure the hook contract is identical. SDKs should expose a single "logSanitizer" interface that both otel and logging hooks call.
devinfra-bot: created: infra/pr-1347 (telemetry: ensure early header sanitization). CI will run lint and unit tests.
Sam L: quick QA check: what should the redacted debug line look like so tests can match?
Mia (devex): expected: 2026-03-21T09:12:11Z DEBUG http.server request_id=[REDACTED] path=/api/complete
Priya (eng-runtime): noted, adding that exact string to the unit test matcher + a trace-level check that shows otel.span retains the trace_id but the request_id field is redacted.
Mia (devex): thanks. I'll update the onboarding doc and include a short troubleshooting snippet showing how to repro locally and how to toggle LOG_LEVEL to avoid leaking during initial setup. :thumbsup:
